lessons: Only defect left: the call_budget ceiling is set once per driver.run, so a re-prompt (RETRY_CAP=1) gets the same full remaining budget as the first call. The Author call has the same bug. Charged spend can exceed $5.00.

Compute each LLMRequest's max_budget_usd when the request is created: GO_SPEND_CAP_USD minus everything charged so far, including earlier calls in the same driver.run. One way is a harness wrapper around llm that tallies result cost per call. Refuse before the call when headroom <= 0.
With a per-request remaining ceiling passed as --max-budget-usd, drop the earlier 'fixed per-call bound' idea. Cost is capped by the provider, so the remaining headroom is itself the bound.

Add a test in test_go_grade.py where a Review reply is invalid, forcing a re-prompt. Assert the second request's max_budget_usd equals the first minus the first call's cost, and total charged <= 5.00. Add the same re-prompt case for Author.

Keep everything review accepted: closed report, KNOWN_ARTIFACTS registration, plant_defects, _run_seq, the go-grade key namespace, the record_go measured summary, --record-go refusal, and the provider --max-budget-usd path. Change only budget propagation and its tests.
Before reporting ok, map each acceptance criterion and review finding to a specific test assertion. Every prior attempt claimed ok well under budget with an open cap defect.
reason: Fifth-plus attempt at the same capability. Each fix for the spend cap has left a new way to overspend, and each run claimed ok early, so more capability is needed to close the cap invariant.
